# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpGX` — SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets a concurrent armed `fa` wipe the live trail

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation fix you listed as the acceptable minimum.

`FileStreamTraceSink`'s class doc (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`) now states the concurrent-run caveat right next to the "ONE trace per file / collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note:

> Concurrent armed runs share that one file: any second armed `fa` boot — another terminal, or a detached child that inherited `FA_STREAM_TRACE` (e.g. `fa dap start` spawning `hub serve`) — truncates the live trail at its install. Copy the file between runs when history matters.

The single-file truncate-per-run design itself is unchanged: it is the documented contract (one trail per run keeps the post-mortem unambiguous, and this PR is a diagnostic whose consumers read the file after a run), and a pid-qualified name or append+header mode would change the contract the two existing tests and the installer docs pin. If a real concurrent-arm workflow shows up, the pid-qualified filename is the natural next step and is now explicitly flagged as the trade-off.

# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpJz` — SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam

**Fixed** in `fbfd318de1` — headless runs now record the render leg, and the docs name both seams.

- `_TerminalCliIO.write` (`bin/fah_io.dart`) — the headless / line-mode live surface (stdout) — now carries the same one-line mark, so `fa -p` / scripted bench runs get the emit→render gap the PR leads with.
- `_TuiCliIO.write` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart`) marks **only its `sendOutput` branch**: when the TUI controller is not attached yet, the write delegates to the raw terminal IO, whose own `write` carries the mark — a surface write fires exactly one `render` line, never two.
- `stream_trace.dart` docs now name both render seams (`_TuiCliIO.write` in TUI mode, `_TerminalCliIO.write` in headless/line-mode runs), so a missing `render` leg can only mean "surface never written", not "TUI-only scope".

On the "render lines are a superset of rendered deltas" point: unchanged by design and now symmetric — both seams mark every primary-surface write (including prompt echo), which is the host-cost the mark exists to name; delta-level attribution comes from the `emit` lines.

Testing note: `_TerminalCliIO` is library-private to `bin/fah.dart` (a `part` file), so it has no direct unit-test seam — the same reason the file has none today. The seam-symmetry change is covered by the CLI suites (`agent_cli_test.dart` 87/87, `ext_cli_test.dart`) passing, and the render contract itself remains pinned by the pure suite (`stream_trace_test.dart`).

# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpL9` — SUGGESTION: `StreamTrace.start` replaces the active trace without releasing the previous sink

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation contract you offered as the alternative to an API change.

`StreamTraceSink` (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart`) now documents the abandonment contract explicitly:

> Sinks must also tolerate being ABANDONED: [StreamTrace.start] replaces the active trace and [StreamTrace.stop] clears it WITHOUT releasing the sink (this interface has no dispose/close hook), so a sink holding resources — `FileStreamTraceSink`'s flush timer, a file handle — must clean up on its own (process exit, or an owner calling its `dispose`).

Rationale for docs over the `onRelease` hook: the trace is started once per process by `maybeStartStreamTrace` (the CLI never re-starts), the only realistic double-`start` is tests, and the Dart SDK test runner disposes the isolate — so the hook would be API surface nobody calls. Sinks that need deterministic cleanup keep `dispose()` for their owners (`FileStreamTraceSink.dispose` cancels the timer and flushes the tail; both trace suites already call it in their fixtures).

**Fixed** in `fbfd318de1` — headless runs now record the render leg, and the docs name both seams.

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation contract you offered as the alternative to an API change.

`StreamTraceSink` (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart`) now documents the abandonment contract explicitly:

> Sinks must also tolerate being ABANDONED: [StreamTrace.start] replaces the active trace and [StreamTrace.stop] clears it WITHOUT releasing the sink (this interface has no dispose/close hook), so a sink holding resources — `FileStreamTraceSink`'s flush timer, a file handle — must clean up on its own (process exit, or an owner calling its `dispose`).

Rationale for docs over the `onRelease` hook: the trace is started once per process by `maybeStartStreamTrace` (the CLI never re-starts), the only realistic double-`start` is tests, and the Dart SDK test runner disposes the isolate — so the hook would be API surface nobody calls. Sinks that need deterministic cleanup keep `dispose()` for their owners (`FileStreamTraceSink.dispose` cancels the timer and flushes the tail; both trace suites already call it in their fixtures).

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpGX` — SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets a concurrent armed `fa` wipe the live trail

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation fix you listed as the acceptable minimum.

`FileStreamTraceSink`'s class doc (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`) now states the concurrent-run caveat right next to the "ONE trace per file / collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note:

> Concurrent armed runs share that one file: any second armed `fa` boot — another terminal, or a detached child that inherited `FA_STREAM_TRACE` (e.g. `fa dap start` spawning `hub serve`) — truncates the live trail at its install. Copy the file between runs when history matters.

The single-file truncate-per-run design itself is unchanged: it is the documented contract (one trail per run keeps the post-mortem unambiguous, and this PR is a diagnostic whose consumers read the file after a run), and a pid-qualified name or append+header mode would change the contract the two existing tests and the installer docs pin. If a real concurrent-arm workflow shows up, the pid-qualified filename is the natural next step and is now explicitly flagged as the trade-off.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_3_suggestion_concurrent_truncate.md"}

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpJz` — SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam

**Fixed** in `fbfd318de1` — headless runs now record the render leg, and the docs name both seams.

- `_TerminalCliIO.write` (`bin/fah_io.dart`) — the headless / line-mode live surface (stdout) — now carries the same one-line mark, so `fa -p` / scripted bench runs get the emit→render gap the PR leads with.
- `_TuiCliIO.write` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart`) marks **only its `sendOutput` branch**: when the TUI controller is not attached yet, the write delegates to the raw terminal IO, whose own `write` carries the mark — a surface write fires exactly one `render` line, never two.
- `stream_trace.dart` docs now name both render seams (`_TuiCliIO.write` in TUI mode, `_TerminalCliIO.write` in headless/line-mode runs), so a missing `render` leg can only mean "surface never written", not "TUI-only scope".

On the "render lines are a superset of rendered deltas" point: unchanged by design and now symmetric — both seams mark every primary-surface write (including prompt echo), which is the host-cost the mark exists to name; delta-level attribution comes from the `emit` lines.

Testing note: `_TerminalCliIO` is library-private to `bin/fah.dart` (a `part` file), so it has no direct unit-test seam — the same reason the file has none today. The seam-symmetry change is covered by the CLI suites (`agent_cli_test.dart` 87/87, `ext_cli_test.dart`) passing, and the render contract itself remains pinned by the pure suite (`stream_trace_test.dart`).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_4_suggestion_headless_render.md"}

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpL9` — SUGGESTION: `StreamTrace.start` replaces the active trace without releasing the previous sink

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation contract you offered as the alternative to an API change.

`StreamTraceSink` (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart`) now documents the abandonment contract explicitly:

> Sinks must also tolerate being ABANDONED: [StreamTrace.start] replaces the active trace and [StreamTrace.stop] clears it WITHOUT releasing the sink (this interface has no dispose/close hook), so a sink holding resources — `FileStreamTraceSink`'s flush timer, a file handle — must clean up on its own (process exit, or an owner calling its `dispose`).

Rationale for docs over the `onRelease` hook: the trace is started once per process by `maybeStartStreamTrace` (the CLI never re-starts), the only realistic double-`start` is tests, and the Dart SDK test runner disposes the isolate — so the hook would be API surface nobody calls. Sinks that need deterministic cleanup keep `dispose()` for their owners (`FileStreamTraceSink.dispose` cancels the timer and flushes the tail; both trace suites already call it in their fixtures).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_5_suggestion_sink_release.md"}

## Rework pass — PR #1727 (`feat/stream-trace`): all 5 open review threads fixed

### Summary

All five open review threads (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 3 SUGGESTIONS) are addressed with code/doc fixes pushed to `feat/stream-trace`, each with a targeted reply in `outputs/review_replies.json`. Two substantive fixes followed TDD (failing test first); CI was green at pass start and no owned CI violations exist.

## Issues/Notes

- **Open threads at pass start: 5** (census `pr_discussions_raw.json`, arm-rule count matches: 5 unresolved). One reply entry + one `.md` per thread under `outputs/review_replies/`.

## Approach

TDD, one thread at a time, committing+pushing each fix immediately:

1. **BLOCKING — armed trace void on fresh installs** (`stream_trace_io.dart:30`): `FileStreamTraceSink` now best-effort creates its parent directory (`_file.parent.createSync(recursive: true)` inside the existing never-throw try/catch, mirroring `FileAgentTelemetrySink.record`) before truncating. RED test first: sink against a not-yet-created nested path failed (zero bytes, silent); GREEN after.
2. **IMPORTANT — `emit` fired once per wrapper hop** (`event_stream.dart:138`): `AssistantMessageEventStream` gained `{bool traced = true}`; the emit switch is guarded by it, and all seven wrapper re-push sites (transient-retry — wrapped around every provider call, DIAL cache probe, silent-stream policy, fallback, provider queue, telemetry, prompt tools) construct with `traced: false`. The five provider adapters keep the default, so `emit` again names the adapter's push and `net→emit` gaps / delta counts are honest. RED tests first (constructor contract + one-emit-per-delta through `transientRetryStreamFunction`: expected 2 `text +` emits / 1 `terminal`, measured 4 / 2 before the fix).
3. **SUGGESTION — concurrent armed run truncates the live trail** (`bin/fah.dart:97`): documented the caveat in `FileStreamTraceSink`'s class doc next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note (your listed minimum): any second armed boot — another terminal or a detached child that inherited `FA_STREAM_TRACE` — truncates the trail; copy the file between runs. Design kept: one trail per run is the pinned contract; pid-qualified names flagged as the next step if a concurrent-arm workflow appears.
4. **SUGGESTION — `render` leg was TUI-only** (`agent_cli_io.dart:102`): wired the same mark into `_TerminalCliIO.write` (headless / line-mode surface), and moved `_TuiCliIO`'s mark into its `sendOutput` branch so a surface write fires exactly one `render` line (the delegate path is marked by the raw terminal IO — never double-counted). Docs now name both seams. Testing note: `_TerminalCliIO` is library-private to `bin/fah.dart` (a `part` file) — no direct unit seam exists today; covered by the CLI suites plus the pure render contract tests.
5. **SUGGESTION — replaced sink never released** (`stream_trace.dart:63`): documented the abandonment contract on `StreamTraceSink` (start/stop never release the sink; resource-holding sinks clean up on their own / via owner-called `dispose`) rather than adding an `onRelease` hook nobody would call — trace starts once per process; tests dispose via the isolate.

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` — parent-dir creation (BLOCKING fix) + concurrent-run caveat docs.
- `lib/src/event_stream.dart` — `traced` flag on `AssistantMessageEventStream` + guarded emit switch + factory passthrough.

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpGX` — SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets a concurrent armed `fa` wipe the live trail

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation fix you listed as the acceptable minimum.

`FileStreamTraceSink`'s class doc (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`) now states the concurrent-run caveat right next to the "ONE trace per file / collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note:

> Concurrent armed runs share that one file: any second armed `fa` boot — another terminal, or a detached child that inherited `FA_STREAM_TRACE` (e.g. `fa dap start` spawning `hub serve`) — truncates the live trail at its install. Copy the file between runs when history matters.

The single-file truncate-per-run design itself is unchanged: it is the documented contract (one trail per run keeps the post-mortem unambiguous, and this PR is a diagnostic whose consumers read the file after a run), and a pid-qualified name or append+header mode would change the contract the two existing tests and the installer docs pin. If a real concurrent-arm workflow shows up, the pid-qualified filename is the natural next step and is now explicitly flagged as the trade-off.

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpJz` — SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam

**Fixed** in `fbfd318de1` — headless runs now record the render leg, and the docs name both seams.

- `_TerminalCliIO.write` (`bin/fah_io.dart`) — the headless / line-mode live surface (stdout) — now carries the same one-line mark, so `fa -p` / scripted bench runs get the emit→render gap the PR leads with.
- `_TuiCliIO.write` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart`) marks **only its `sendOutput` branch**: when the TUI controller is not attached yet, the write delegates to the raw terminal IO, whose own `write` carries the mark — a surface write fires exactly one `render` line, never two.
- `stream_trace.dart` docs now name both render seams (`_TuiCliIO.write` in TUI mode, `_TerminalCliIO.write` in headless/line-mode runs), so a missing `render` leg can only mean "surface never written", not "TUI-only scope".

On the "render lines are a superset of rendered deltas" point: unchanged by design and now symmetric — both seams mark every primary-surface write (including prompt echo), which is the host-cost the mark exists to name; delta-level attribution comes from the `emit` lines.

Testing note: `_TerminalCliIO` is library-private to `bin/fah.dart` (a `part` file), so it has no direct unit-test seam — the same reason the file has none today. The seam-symmetry change is covered by the CLI suites (`agent_cli_test.dart` 87/87, `ext_cli_test.dart`) passing, and the render contract itself remains pinned by the pure suite (`stream_trace_test.dart`).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_4_suggestion_headless_render.md"}

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpL9` — SUGGESTION: `StreamTrace.start` replaces the active trace without releasing the previous sink

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation contract you offered as the alternative to an API change.

`StreamTraceSink` (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart`) now documents the abandonment contract explicitly:

> Sinks must also tolerate being ABANDONED: [StreamTrace.start] replaces the active trace and [StreamTrace.stop] clears it WITHOUT releasing the sink (this interface has no dispose/close hook), so a sink holding resources — `FileStreamTraceSink`'s flush timer, a file handle — must clean up on its own (process exit, or an owner calling its `dispose`).

Rationale for docs over the `onRelease` hook: the trace is started once per process by `maybeStartStreamTrace` (the CLI never re-starts), the only realistic double-`start` is tests, and the Dart SDK test runner disposes the isolate — so the hook would be API surface nobody calls. Sinks that need deterministic cleanup keep `dispose()` for their owners (`FileStreamTraceSink.dispose` cancels the timer and flushes the tail; both trace suites already call it in their fixtures).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_5_suggestion_sink_release.md"}

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpGX` — SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets a concurrent armed `fa` wipe the live trail

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation fix you listed as the acceptable minimum.

`FileStreamTraceSink`'s class doc (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`) now states the concurrent-run caveat right next to the "ONE trace per file / collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note:

> Concurrent armed runs share that one file: any second armed `fa` boot — another terminal, or a detached child that inherited `FA_STREAM_TRACE` (e.g. `fa dap start` spawning `hub serve`) — truncates the live trail at its install. Copy the file between runs when history matters.

The single-file truncate-per-run design itself is unchanged: it is the documented contract (one trail per run keeps the post-mortem unambiguous, and this PR is a diagnostic whose consumers read the file after a run), and a pid-qualified name or append+header mode would change the contract the two existing tests and the installer docs pin. If a real concurrent-arm workflow shows up, the pid-qualified filename is the natural next step and is now explicitly flagged as the trade-off.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_3_suggestion_concurrent_truncate.md"}

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpJz` — SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam

**Fixed** in `fbfd318de1` — headless runs now record the render leg, and the docs name both seams.

- `_TerminalCliIO.write` (`bin/fah_io.dart`) — the headless / line-mode live surface (stdout) — now carries the same one-line mark, so `fa -p` / scripted bench runs get the emit→render gap the PR leads with.
- `_TuiCliIO.write` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart`) marks **only its `sendOutput` branch**: when the TUI controller is not attached yet, the write delegates to the raw terminal IO, whose own `write` carries the mark — a surface write fires exactly one `render` line, never two.
- `stream_trace.dart` docs now name both render seams (`_TuiCliIO.write` in TUI mode, `_TerminalCliIO.write` in headless/line-mode runs), so a missing `render` leg can only mean "surface never written", not "TUI-only scope".

On the "render lines are a superset of rendered deltas" point: unchanged by design and now symmetric — both seams mark every primary-surface write (including prompt echo), which is the host-cost the mark exists to name; delta-level attribution comes from the `emit` lines.

Testing note: `_TerminalCliIO` is library-private to `bin/fah.dart` (a `part` file), so it has no direct unit-test seam — the same reason the file has none today. The seam-symmetry change is covered by the CLI suites (`agent_cli_test.dart` 87/87, `ext_cli_test.dart`) passing, and the render contract itself remains pinned by the pure suite (`stream_trace_test.dart`).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_4_suggestion_headless_render.md"}

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpL9` — SUGGESTION: `StreamTrace.start` replaces the active trace without releasing the previous sink

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation contract you offered as the alternative to an API change.

`StreamTraceSink` (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart`) now documents the abandonment contract explicitly:

> Sinks must also tolerate being ABANDONED: [StreamTrace.start] replaces the active trace and [StreamTrace.stop] clears it WITHOUT releasing the sink (this interface has no dispose/close hook), so a sink holding resources — `FileStreamTraceSink`'s flush timer, a file handle — must clean up on its own (process exit, or an owner calling its `dispose`).

Rationale for docs over the `onRelease` hook: the trace is started once per process by `maybeStartStreamTrace` (the CLI never re-starts), the only realistic double-`start` is tests, and the Dart SDK test runner disposes the isolate — so the hook would be API surface nobody calls. Sinks that need deterministic cleanup keep `dispose()` for their owners (`FileStreamTraceSink.dispose` cancels the timer and flushes the tail; both trace suites already call it in their fixtures).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_5_suggestion_sink_release.md"}

`StreamTraceSink` (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart`) now documents the abandonment contract explicitly:

> Sinks must also tolerate being ABANDONED: [StreamTrace.start] replaces the active trace and [StreamTrace.stop] clears it WITHOUT releasing the sink (this interface has no dispose/close hook), so a sink holding resources — `FileStreamTraceSink`'s flush timer, a file handle — must clean up on its own (process exit, or an owner calling its `dispose`).

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpGX` — SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets a concurrent armed `fa` wipe the live trail

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation fix you listed as the acceptable minimum.

`FileStreamTraceSink`'s class doc (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`) now states the concurrent-run caveat right next to the "ONE trace per file / collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note:

> Concurrent armed runs share that one file: any second armed `fa` boot — another terminal, or a detached child that inherited `FA_STREAM_TRACE` (e.g. `fa dap start` spawning `hub serve`) — truncates the live trail at its install. Copy the file between runs when history matters.

The single-file truncate-per-run design itself is unchanged: it is the documented contract (one trail per run keeps the post-mortem unambiguous, and this PR is a diagnostic whose consumers read the file after a run), and a pid-qualified name or append+header mode would change the contract the two existing tests and the installer docs pin. If a real concurrent-arm workflow shows up, the pid-qualified filename is the natural next step and is now explicitly flagged as the trade-off.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_3_suggestion_concurrent_truncate.md"}

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpJz` — SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam

**Fixed** in `fbfd318de1` — headless runs now record the render leg, and the docs name both seams.

- `_TerminalCliIO.write` (`bin/fah_io.dart`) — the headless / line-mode live surface (stdout) — now carries the same one-line mark, so `fa -p` / scripted bench runs get the emit→render gap the PR leads with.
- `_TuiCliIO.write` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart`) marks **only its `sendOutput` branch**: when the TUI controller is not attached yet, the write delegates to the raw terminal IO, whose own `write` carries the mark — a surface write fires exactly one `render` line, never two.
- `stream_trace.dart` docs now name both render seams (`_TuiCliIO.write` in TUI mode, `_TerminalCliIO.write` in headless/line-mode runs), so a missing `render` leg can only mean "surface never written", not "TUI-only scope".

On the "render lines are a superset of rendered deltas" point: unchanged by design and now symmetric — both seams mark every primary-surface write (including prompt echo), which is the host-cost the mark exists to name; delta-level attribution comes from the `emit` lines.

Testing note: `_TerminalCliIO` is library-private to `bin/fah.dart` (a `part` file), so it has no direct unit-test seam — the same reason the file has none today. The seam-symmetry change is covered by the CLI suites (`agent_cli_test.dart` 87/87, `ext_cli_test.dart`) passing, and the render contract itself remains pinned by the pure suite (`stream_trace_test.dart`).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_4_suggestion_headless_render.md"}

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpL9` — SUGGESTION: `StreamTrace.start` replaces the active trace without releasing the previous sink

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation contract you offered as the alternative to an API change.

`StreamTraceSink` (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart`) now documents the abandonment contract explicitly:

> Sinks must also tolerate being ABANDONED: [StreamTrace.start] replaces the active trace and [StreamTrace.stop] clears it WITHOUT releasing the sink (this interface has no dispose/close hook), so a sink holding resources — `FileStreamTraceSink`'s flush timer, a file handle — must clean up on its own (process exit, or an owner calling its `dispose`).

Rationale for docs over the `onRelease` hook: the trace is started once per process by `maybeStartStreamTrace` (the CLI never re-starts), the only realistic double-`start` is tests, and the Dart SDK test runner disposes the isolate — so the hook would be API surface nobody calls. Sinks that need deterministic cleanup keep `dispose()` for their owners (`FileStreamTraceSink.dispose` cancels the timer and flushes the tail; both trace suites already call it in their fixtures).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_5_suggestion_sink_release.md"}

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation contract you offered as the alternative to an API change.

`StreamTraceSink` (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart`) now documents the abandonment contract explicitly:

> Sinks must also tolerate being ABANDONED: [StreamTrace.start] replaces the active trace and [StreamTrace.stop] clears it WITHOUT releasing the sink (this interface has no dispose/close hook), so a sink holding resources — `FileStreamTraceSink`'s flush timer, a file handle — must clean up on its own (process exit, or an owner calling its `dispose`).

Rationale for docs over the `onRelease` hook: the trace is started once per process by `maybeStartStreamTrace` (the CLI never re-starts), the only realistic double-`start` is tests, and the Dart SDK test runner disposes the isolate — so the hook would be API surface nobody calls. {"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpGX` — SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets a concurrent armed `fa` wipe the live trail

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation fix you listed as the acceptable minimum.

`FileStreamTraceSink`'s class doc (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`) now states the concurrent-run caveat right next to the "ONE trace per file / collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note:

> Concurrent armed runs share that one file: any second armed `fa` boot — another terminal, or a detached child that inherited `FA_STREAM_TRACE` (e.g. `fa dap start` spawning `hub serve`) — truncates the live trail at its install. Copy the file between runs when history matters.

The single-file truncate-per-run design itself is unchanged: it is the documented contract (one trail per run keeps the post-mortem unambiguous, and this PR is a diagnostic whose consumers read the file after a run), and a pid-qualified name or append+header mode would change the contract the two existing tests and the installer docs pin. If a real concurrent-arm workflow shows up, the pid-qualified filename is the natural next step and is now explicitly flagged as the trade-off.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_3_suggestion_concurrent_truncate.md"}

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpJz` — SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam

**Fixed** in `fbfd318de1` — headless runs now record the render leg, and the docs name both seams.

- `_TerminalCliIO.write` (`bin/fah_io.dart`) — the headless / line-mode live surface (stdout) — now carries the same one-line mark, so `fa -p` / scripted bench runs get the emit→render gap the PR leads with.
- `_TuiCliIO.write` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart`) marks **only its `sendOutput` branch**: when the TUI controller is not attached yet, the write delegates to the raw terminal IO, whose own `write` carries the mark — a surface write fires exactly one `render` line, never two.
- `stream_trace.dart` docs now name both render seams (`_TuiCliIO.write` in TUI mode, `_TerminalCliIO.write` in headless/line-mode runs), so a missing `render` leg can only mean "surface never written", not "TUI-only scope".

On the "render lines are a superset of rendered deltas" point: unchanged by design and now symmetric — both seams mark every primary-surface write (including prompt echo), which is the host-cost the mark exists to name; delta-level attribution comes from the `emit` lines.

Testing note: `_TerminalCliIO` is library-private to `bin/fah.dart` (a `part` file), so it has no direct unit-test seam — the same reason the file has none today. The seam-symmetry change is covered by the CLI suites (`agent_cli_test.dart` 87/87, `ext_cli_test.dart`) passing, and the render contract itself remains pinned by the pure suite (`stream_trace_test.dart`).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_4_suggestion_headless_render.md"}

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpL9` — SUGGESTION: `StreamTrace.start` replaces the active trace without releasing the previous sink

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation contract you offered as the alternative to an API change.

`StreamTraceSink` (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart`) now documents the abandonment contract explicitly:

> Sinks must also tolerate being ABANDONED: [StreamTrace.start] replaces the active trace and [StreamTrace.stop] clears it WITHOUT releasing the sink (this interface has no dispose/close hook), so a sink holding resources — `FileStreamTraceSink`'s flush timer, a file handle — must clean up on its own (process exit, or an owner calling its `dispose`).

Rationale for docs over the `onRelease` hook: the trace is started once per process by `maybeStartStreamTrace` (the CLI never re-starts), the only realistic double-`start` is tests, and the Dart SDK test runner disposes the isolate — so the hook would be API surface nobody calls. Sinks that need deterministic cleanup keep `dispose()` for their owners (`FileStreamTraceSink.dispose` cancels the timer and flushes the tail; both trace suites already call it in their fixtures).

TDD, one thread at a time, committing+pushing each fix immediately:

1. **BLOCKING — armed trace void on fresh installs** (`stream_trace_io.dart:30`): `FileStreamTraceSink` now best-effort creates its parent directory (`_file.parent.createSync(recursive: true)` inside the existing never-throw try/catch, mirroring `FileAgentTelemetrySink.record`) before truncating. **Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation contract you offered as the alternative to an API change.

`StreamTraceSink` (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart`) now documents the abandonment contract explicitly:

> Sinks must also tolerate being ABANDONED: [StreamTrace.start] replaces the active trace and [StreamTrace.stop] clears it WITHOUT releasing the sink (this interface has no dispose/close hook), so a sink holding resources — `FileStreamTraceSink`'s flush timer, a file handle — must clean up on its own (process exit, or an owner calling its `dispose`).

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpGX` — SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets a concurrent armed `fa` wipe the live trail

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation fix you listed as the acceptable minimum.

`FileStreamTraceSink`'s class doc (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`) now states the concurrent-run caveat right next to the "ONE trace per file / collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note:

> Concurrent armed runs share that one file: any second armed `fa` boot — another terminal, or a detached child that inherited `FA_STREAM_TRACE` (e.g. `fa dap start` spawning `hub serve`) — truncates the live trail at its install. Copy the file between runs when history matters.

The single-file truncate-per-run design itself is unchanged: it is the documented contract (one trail per run keeps the post-mortem unambiguous, and this PR is a diagnostic whose consumers read the file after a run), and a pid-qualified name or append+header mode would change the contract the two existing tests and the installer docs pin. If a real concurrent-arm workflow shows up, the pid-qualified filename is the natural next step and is now explicitly flagged as the trade-off.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_3_suggestion_concurrent_truncate.md"}

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpJz` — SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam

**Fixed** in `fbfd318de1` — headless runs now record the render leg, and the docs name both seams.

- `_TerminalCliIO.write` (`bin/fah_io.dart`) — the headless / line-mode live surface (stdout) — now carries the same one-line mark, so `fa -p` / scripted bench runs get the emit→render gap the PR leads with.
- `_TuiCliIO.write` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart`) marks **only its `sendOutput` branch**: when the TUI controller is not attached yet, the write delegates to the raw terminal IO, whose own `write` carries the mark — a surface write fires exactly one `render` line, never two.
- `stream_trace.dart` docs now name both render seams (`_TuiCliIO.write` in TUI mode, `_TerminalCliIO.write` in headless/line-mode runs), so a missing `render` leg can only mean "surface never written", not "TUI-only scope".

On the "render lines are a superset of rendered deltas" point: unchanged by design and now symmetric — both seams mark every primary-surface write (including prompt echo), which is the host-cost the mark exists to name; delta-level attribution comes from the `emit` lines.

Testing note: `_TerminalCliIO` is library-private to `bin/fah.dart` (a `part` file), so it has no direct unit-test seam — the same reason the file has none today. The seam-symmetry change is covered by the CLI suites (`agent_cli_test.dart` 87/87, `ext_cli_test.dart`) passing, and the render contract itself remains pinned by the pure suite (`stream_trace_test.dart`).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_4_suggestion_headless_render.md"}

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uhpL9` — SUGGESTION: `StreamTrace.start` replaces the active trace without releasing the previous sink

**Addressed** in `fbfd318de1` via the documentation contract you offered as the alternative to an API change.

`StreamTraceSink` (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart`) now documents the abandonment contract explicitly:

> Sinks must also tolerate being ABANDONED: [StreamTrace.start] replaces the active trace and [StreamTrace.stop] clears it WITHOUT releasing the sink (this interface has no dispose/close hook), so a sink holding resources — `FileStreamTraceSink`'s flush timer, a file handle — must clean up on its own (process exit, or an owner calling its `dispose`).

Rationale for docs over the `onRelease` hook: the trace is started once per process by `maybeStartStreamTrace` (the CLI never re-starts), the only realistic double-`start` is tests, and the Dart SDK test runner disposes the isolate — so the hook would be API surface nobody calls. Sinks that need deterministic cleanup keep `dispose()` for their owners (`FileStreamTraceSink.dispose` cancels the timer and flushes the tail; both trace suites already call it in their fixtures).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_5_suggestion_sink_release.md"}

`StreamTraceSink` (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart`) now documents the abandonment contract explicitly:

> Sinks must also tolerate being ABANDONED: [StreamTrace.start] replaces the active trace and [StreamTrace.stop] clears it WITHOUT releasing the sink (this interface has no dispose/close hook), so a sink holding resources — `FileStreamTraceSink`'s flush timer, a file handle — must clean up on its own (process exit, or an owner calling its `dispose`).

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All findings fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["PR Rework TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it"] R2["✅ If the existing tests only cover a single-item/simple case, add a test for the multi-item/edge case the finding points at — a fix without a test for that exact case is not verified"] R3["✅ Returned findings: your fix must differ from the previous attempt and the new/updated test must prove it"] R4["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] R5["✅ Verification order: finalize ALL fixes BEFORE launching the full test-suite/coverage run — a run over a tree you are still editing is wasted"] R6["✅ Long runs (full suite, coverage) start with bash background: true and are collected via bash_job status/output between other steps — NEVER foreground sleep-polling (see prompts/bash_tools.md)"] R7["❌ NEVER kill a running verification because files changed after it started — let it finish, treat the result as stale, re-run deliberately"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## formatting_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md must be Markdown (# headings, - bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check same pattern across codebase"] F4["Do NOT refactor unrelated code or add unrequested features"] F5["When open PR review threads exist, create outputs/review_replies/*.md files and reference them from outputs/review_replies.json"] ``` - When `input//pr_discussions_raw.json` contains open PR review threads: - Write one Markdown file per open thread under `outputs/review_replies/`. - Write `outputs/review_replies.json` with one entry per open thread, including `inReplyToId`, `threadId`, and a `reply` field that contains the path to the matching `.md` file. - Do **not** put reply bodies inline in the JSON. ## output_rules.md ## PR Rework — Output Rules Rework posts **only** to the Pull Request. All output must be Markdown. ### Required files 1. `outputs/response.md` - Markdown fix summary for the top-level PR comment. - Use `#`/`##` headings, ` ``` ` code fences, `-` bullets. - Required sections: `## Issues/Notes`, `## Approach`, `## Files Modified`, `## Test Coverage`. - **Owned CI violations**: when `ci_failures.md` has a "Violations you must fix (N owned)" table, list EVERY owned violation with `fixed` (what changed) or `disputed: ` (why the gate is wrong). A summary claiming the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected — the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts it. 2. `outputs/review_replies.json` - **Mandatory** when the PR has open review threads. - If there are no open threads, write `{ "replies": [] }`. - Format: ```json { "replies": [ { "inReplyToId": 1234567890, "threadId": "", "reply": "outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md" } ] } ``` 3. `outputs/review_replies/*.md` - One Markdown file per open PR review thread. - The file path is referenced from `outputs/review_replies.json` via the `reply` field. - Keep each reply concise and factual; reference the fix location when possible. Rules for review replies: - Read `input//pr_discussions_raw.json` to obtain each open thread's `threadId` and `rootCommentId` (`inReplyToId`). - Create one reply entry and one `.md` file for **every** open review thread — do not skip any unresolved conversation. - `threadId` is required to resolve/close the conversation; `inReplyToId` is required to post the reply in the correct thread. - ⚠️ **Copy `threadId` verbatim, character-for-character, from `pr_discussions_raw.json`.** Its format depends on which SCM the PR lives on (a GitHub GraphQL node ID, a GitLab discussion hash, an ADO thread number, etc.) and is opaque — never invent, prefix, reformat, or pattern-match it against an example. The value above is a placeholder showing *where* the field goes, not what it should look like. - Do **not** put the reply body inline in the JSON; use the `reply` field only as a file path reference. - ⚠️ **Common mistake**: `pr_discussions_raw.json` uses the field names `rootCommentId` and `body`. When writing `review_replies.json`, you MUST rename these to `inReplyToId` and `reply` respectively — do NOT copy the input field names as-is into the output JSON, or the reply will silently post as an untargeted top-level comment instead of a threaded reply. ### Blocked (agents#827) Rework only reworks: it fixes the open review threads in code and never asks questions (questions belong to the refinement agents). Every open thread needs a code fix in this pass. If you hit a problem you genuinely cannot get past, change no thread state and write the reason in `outputs/response.md` (start the file with `BLOCKED:` followed by what blocks you and what is needed). A pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked: threads are not resolved and the ticket moves to the Blocked status. Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write `outputs/response.md` — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise. ## github_comment_format.md # GitHub tracker comment Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every construct must render natively on GitHub. - Headings: `##`, `###` - Bullets: `- item` - Numbered lists: `1. item` - Bold: `**text**` - Inline code: `` `code` `` - Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`) - Link: `[text](url)` - Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row) Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks, no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no `{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable. **IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues, get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER` (the composite key form works directly). ## dmtools_cli.md ## DMTools CLI — External Data Access > **PR Review note**: Ticket/PR context is pre-loaded. Use dmtools only for additional data (e.g., parent story details, linked tickets not in input/). dmtools jira_get_ticket PROJ-456 [jira-ticket]

dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL"] -.-> NEED ``` ## bash_tools.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph USE["Use dmtools skill"] U1["Jira, Figma, Confluence, Teams, etc."] U2["Credentials preconfigured via environment variables"] end subgraph SHELLSTATE["⚠️ Persistent-shell pitfalls (sandbox-observed)"] P1["Never end commands with exit — it kills the shell session, making read_bash fail with Invalid shell ID"] P2["Capture the exit code via $? right after the command, before running anything else — a late $? reads the wrong command's code"] P3["Avoid $PIPESTATUS — it produced wrong exit codes in the sandbox; redirect output to a file and check $? instead"] end subgraph CWD["Working directory discipline (persistent shell!)"] C1["Your Bash shell is ONE persistent session for the whole task — a cd in one command carries over to every later command, including Write/Edit"] C2["cd dependencies/<repo> to explore a dependency's source? You are now inside it for every subsequent command until you cd out"] C3["Forgetting to cd back before writing outputs/* silently writes to dependencies/<repo>/outputs/* instead of the job's own outputs/ — the write itself succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, but the file is lost"] C4["Before ANY Write/Edit to outputs/ (response.md, pr_review.json, pr_review_comments/*.md, etc.): run pwd first and confirm you are at the job root, not inside dependencies/"] C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"] C6["Do NOT defensively re-cd into a directory you are already in — running cd dependencies/<repo> a second time while already inside it fails with No such file or directory (it looks for a nested dependencies/<repo>/dependencies/<repo>).
